problem: Audio-visual navigation backbones (CNN audio encoder + GRU state encoder, as in AV-WaN) have not changed since 2020. GRUs dilute critical acoustic cues with redundant observations, and CNNs have a local bias that breaks global time-frequency dependencies in spectrograms.
motivation: Backbone-level representation limits are argued to bottleneck AVN performance, while most prior work only improves multimodal fusion. Mamba's selective state-space scan offers content-aware, linear-complexity sequence modeling, which could fix both state dilution and spectrogram fragmentation.
key_idea: Replace the GRU with a selective-scan Mamba State Encoder and the CNN audio encoder with a bidirectional Audio Mamba Encoder in the AV-WaN waypoint framework, keeping a CNN for the visual branch.
insight: Ablations show the audio encoder matters most on Replica: reverting AME to CNN drops unheard SR from 72.8 to 59.0, while reverting M-SE only drops it to 71.0. On MP3D both modules contribute (unheard SR 62.6 w/o AME, 60.2 w/o M-SE, versus 68.0 full). Heard-setting results on Replica are mixed: the ablated variants are sometimes better than the full model, and AV-WaN beats Samba there. The gains are therefore mainly in generalization to unheard sounds, and parameters go down (Samba 10.5M vs AV-WaN 11.2M on Replica, 4.6M vs 5.6M on MP3D).
method: Audio Mamba Encoder (AME): flattens the binaural spectrogram (channel x frequency) per time step into tokens, projects them with Linear+LN+ReLU, adds temporal positional embeddings, and runs stacked Mamba layers with alternating time-axis flips (bidirectional). Mean pooling and a linear head give the audio vector b_t.

Mamba State Encoder (M-SE): replaces the GRU. It uses linear projection + local 1D conv, then a selective SSM whose Δ, B, C are input-dependent. Recurrence h_t = Ā h_{t-1} + B̄ x_t, with simplified discretization Ā=exp(ΔA), B̄=ΔB. A gated residual path produces the global state h_t.

Dual-mode execution: parallel scan for training over long sequences, single-step recurrent mode for deployment. State and conv buffers are packed/unpacked, and the hidden state is reset via masks at episode ends for PPO stability.

Waypoint policy pipeline (AV-WaN-style): depth-derived geometric vector, acoustic map feature a_t and global map G_t feed M-SE; an actor-critic trained with PPO samples waypoints (Δx,Δy) on an action map, and a path planner executes them.
Hybrid design: the CNN is kept in the visual (depth) branch for spatial inductive bias, and Mamba is used only for audio and temporal state.

setting.backbone: AV-WaN-style waypoint policy with Audio Mamba Encoder + Mamba State Encoder + CNN depth encoder (trained from scratch with PPO)
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces on Replica and Matterport3D; 102 sounds (78 train / 11 val / 18 test for unheard); heard = telephone ringtone; RL from scratch, no extra data
setting.observation: Depth image + binaural spectrogram + accumulated geometric and acoustic maps
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints (Δx,Δy) on an action map, executed by a path planner
setting.privileged: none stated (global geometric map is built by the agent)

numbers_note: The split is described as unseen test scenes; the paper does not give a formal split name, so 'test' is used. Results are for the Depth setting only.
results: Samba beats AV-WaN in most settings. On Replica unheard it reaches SR 72.8 vs 52.8 (SPL 42.4 vs 34.7), and on MP3D unheard SR 68.0 vs 56.7 and SPL 47.1 vs 40.9. On heard Replica, AV-WaN remains better (SR 98.7 vs 93.4). Samba also has fewer parameters (4.6M vs 5.6M on MP3D).
limitations: Only simulated SoundSpaces (Replica, MP3D) with the Depth setting; no real-robot tests and no comparison to recent stronger AVN methods.
Claim of 'outperforming all baselines across all environments' is contradicted by Replica Heard, where AV-WaN is better; Replica heard ablations show the full model is not uniformly best.

The abstract claims an 11.3% SR gain on MP3D but the table shows a gain of 11.3 points only on unheard; the simplified discretization (B̄=ΔB) and latency claims are not validated with speed measurements.
